{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "High frequency of vital signs and lab tests at every weekly visit",
      "quote": "Vital signs will be conducted as specified in the Schedule of Assessments (Table 1).",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "7.1.8 Vital Signs",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Vital signs and clinical laboratory tests are scheduled at every weekly visit (W1D1 through W7D1 and Q3W), which is burdensome for patients and sites, especially for a study with weekly intratumoral injections.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing vital signs and lab tests to every other week or at key timepoints (e.g., before each cycle) to reduce patient burden."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tumor biopsy at W5D1 may be unnecessary",
      "quote": "Tumor Biopsyq | X |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "A tumor biopsy is scheduled at W5D1 in addition to screening. This is an invasive procedure that adds significant patient burden and may be difficult to collect, especially if the tumor is not easily accessible.",
      "fix": "Consider eliminating the W5D1 biopsy or making it optional, or align it with a clinically indicated procedure."
    },
    {
      "title": "Pharmacokinetic sampling at W6D2 and W7D1 may be redundant",
      "quote": "Pharmacokinetic Samplingn |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PK sampling is scheduled at W6D2 and W7D1, which are consecutive days. This may be unnecessary and burdensome for patients who must return for an extra visit.",
      "fix": "Consider consolidating PK sampling to a single timepoint or reducing the number of PK samples."
    },
    {
      "title": "Disease assessment at EOT and PTFU may be too frequent",
      "quote": "Disease Assessment (radiographic imaging)r | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  | X |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Radiographic imaging is scheduled at EOT and then every 3 months during posttreatment follow-up. This is standard but may be burdensome for patients with stable disease; consider less frequent imaging if clinically appropriate.",
      "fix": "Consider imaging every 6 months for patients with stable disease after EOT."
    },
    {
      "title": "Screening window of 30 days may be too long for some assessments",
      "quote": "Screening (Day -30 to Day -1) (Day -30)",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The screening window is 30 days, which is long and may lead to out-of-date lab results or disease progression before baseline. Also, the physical exam must be within 72 hours of W1D1, but other screening assessments may be older.",
      "fix": "Consider shortening the screening window to 21 or 28 days, or specify that key eligibility labs must be within a shorter window."
    },
    {
      "title": "Physical exam frequency may be excessive",
      "quote": "Physical Examinationg | X | X |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X |  |  |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Physical exams are scheduled at W1D1, W3D1, W7D1, and every Q3W visit. This is frequent and may be burdensome, especially for a study with weekly injections.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing physical exams to every other cycle or as clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "Adverse event monitoring and concomitant meds recorded at every visit including follow-up",
      "quote": "Adverse Event Monitoringi | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "AE and concomitant medication monitoring is recorded at every visit, including long-term survival follow-up phone calls. This is standard but may be burdensome for sites during long-term follow-up.",
      "fix": "Consider limiting AE and concomitant medication recording to treatment period and 100-day follow-up, and only collect serious AEs and related meds during long-term follow-up."
    },
    {
      "title": "Immunogenicity sampling at EOT and PTFU may be unnecessary",
      "quote": "Immunogenicity Samplingp | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  | X |  | X |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Immunogenicity sampling is scheduled at EOT and at every posttreatment follow-up visit (Q3mo). This adds patient burden and may not be necessary at every follow-up visit.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing immunogenicity sampling to EOT and 100-day follow-up only, or at longer intervals."
    }
  ]
}
